name: matched-gaussian-camp-comparison

world.sampling: same fixed signal plus independent Gaussian sensor noise, not samples from the candidate DAGs

references.source: unchanged combustion world, original candidate means and covariances
references.marginalization: first marginalize each candidate to C,G,M; never pool distinct hidden P/O coordinates
references.info: equal average of observable marginal precision matrices and information vectors
references.moment: Gaussian with mean and covariance of equal-weight observable candidate mixture, including between-mean covariance
references.initialization: every agent starts at the same shared K=1 reference in each condition; no camp-specific anchor

gate.z2: sum over C,G,M of squared entering-mean differences divided by 1/Pi_i[v,v] + 1/Pi_j[v,v]
gate.normalization: exact positive row denominator, no epsilon mass deficit; positive self weight guarantees denominator
gate.timing: entering-state means, before communication and observation
gate.scope: conditional social sharing only; no sensory gate, model support gate, utility or model-score forgetting
gate.readout: retain per-agent realized total weight assigned to opposite group

pairing.rng: JAX threefry2x32; key,sk=split(key), agent_keys=split(sk,N); seed initializes PRNGKey
pairing.evaluation: fold_in(entering_key,314159); normal((N,4,3),float64), never enters training state
pairing.claim: paired extension of existing seed streams, not new independent confirmation of candidate outcomes

analysis.distance: Euclidean distance between camp averages of observable posterior predictive means; candidate mixture primary, MAP secondary
analysis.signed_difference: gas camp minus mass camp on C,G,M
analysis.systematic_gap: within each seed average signed difference over window before taking norm; distinguish mean instantaneous norm and norm after across-seed averaging
analysis.performance: per-group full observable signal MSE and independent held-out Gaussian/mixture NLL, both tail and endpoint
contrasts: moment-minus-information reference within each Gaussian mechanism
analysis.unit: whole seed, paired across arms; pointwise 95% percentile intervals
analysis.gate_diagnostics: effective cross-group conditional influence, reported separately for each group
analysis.across_seed_norm: norm of across-seed average signed gap is a descriptive point only; no percentile CI or significance inference from its nonnegative norm; report signed coordinates separately

figure_plan.main: old-style camp predictive distance with Gaussian, gated Gaussian, private candidate and shared-weight candidate control; candidate q by group; late predictive losses including gas-variance control
figure_plan.supplement: reference-compression sensitivity, MAP vs mixture distance, systematic vs instantaneous gap, effective cross-group influence
figure_plan.style: orx vendored style, actual LaTeX Computer Modern, 4.8in vector PDF/SVG plus PNG preview

interpretation_limits: Matched retention and information access do not make the K=1 prior identical to a two-component mixture.
Continuous prediction disagreement is not opposing theoretical commitment.
Continual heterogeneous observations plus reference retention can sustain a single-Gaussian gap.
The private-weight candidate condition does not exchange model support; shared-weight control must be visible.
Gate nu inherited from archived experiment, not tuned to the resulting trajectories.
Variance control and predictive costs remain part of any camp-separation claim.
validation_plan: independent prior compilation and expected stationary means for ungated K1
independent NumPy per-step score/deposit/retention and full-observation predictive NLL
paired observation/evaluation hashes vs archived C10
restart equivalence and no RNG consumption by readouts
raw finiteness positive definiteness, all hashes and checkpoint continuity
independent reductions of scalar and gap statistics
